name: Terminal Root Cycles Couple as Two-Sided Passive-Gate Holonomy
statement: Let $\mathscr S$ be the distinct nonempty proper passive shores of a two-sided terminal fiber. It is nonempty. For each $S\in\mathscr S$, choose a two-block peeling with first lower root $r_S\in R\cap S$ and last upper root $u_S\in R^+\cap(D\setminus S)$. There are self-maps $\lambda,\mu$ of $\mathscr S$ such that $r_S\in S\setminus\lambda(S)$ and $u_S\in\mu(S)\setminus S$. Neither map has a fixed point, so both contain directed cycles. If there are exactly two shores $S,T$, then $r_S,u_T\in S\setminus T$ and $r_T,u_S\in T\setminus S$.
proof: A lower root has a nonempty proper blocker shore, proving $\mathscr S$ nonempty. Passive-shore absorption supplies the two-block peeling and its endpoint roots. Apply the blocker-cell theorem to $r_S$ and define $\lambda(S)$ to be a shore omitting it; apply the complementary theorem to $u_S$ and define $\mu(S)$ to be a shore containing it while the opposite shore omits it. The asymmetric differences forbid fixed points, and finite fixed-point-free self-maps contain cycles. On a two-element shore set both maps interchange the shores, giving the crossed profile.
